parts:
The updated note is in your smooth-poincare-4d folder at `papers/master/brainstorm/notes/claude/PATHS_FORWARD_AFTER_ATTAINMENT_AND_ENTRY_TRIALS_20261126.md`, with a `_checks` folder beside it (four scripts, 75 checks, all pass). Nothing in it has been read by a specialist, and I did not audit the proof in 06.

Its main conclusions:

- **Attainment (06) comes first.** It is the one result that keeps its value whatever is true about exotic spheres, and it has only been read inside the pipeline. I recommend a specialist reading, a standalone paper and published imports before any new sub-investigation.
- **Entry (07) is blocked by the design, not the presentation.** Every negative result in 07 is an instance of one inequality: each thin relator tube costs at least 16π²/3 per sign, against a total budget of 8π², unless a certain doubled manifold is strongly Yamabe-negative. In that remaining case, an entering trial in the 07 family, including the open full-width one, would give a conformal class on S²×S² with less Weyl energy than the Einstein product. That would contradict Kobayashi's 1985 conjecture, which is open, so the result is conditional. One eigenvalue sign per tube would make the closure unconditional.
- **The same holds for the trivial presentation.** Drawn with the same thin tubes it cannot enter either, while with fat caps it enters at 4.13π² in a rotationally symmetric model. Handles must be fat to be cheap.
- **Rigidity is a sphere theorem with no known mechanism.** Given attainment, it is equivalent to a statement that contains "a homotopy four-sphere with a positive Einstein metric is standard". I suggest naming it as a conjecture and working two sub-cases only.
- **05's slide enumeration should stop.** By Gompf–Scharlemann–Thompson, success at n=3 would trivialise the Akbulut–Kirby presentation, and a bounded failure proves nothing.

The note also has an order of work with stop rules, and it accepts the pipeline's correction to the Gluck section of my earlier note.

Beyond the note and its checks, I recorded this session as entry 2 in `papers/master/chat-histories/claude-cowork` (new record, `index.json`, README) and saved a copy of the note to the project. Nothing was committed to git. The earlier brainstorm session that wrote `ENTRY_DIRECT_APPROACHES_20261126.md` has no entry in any Claude registry.

parts:
The master manuscript now carries the additions: three new input files in `papers/master/manuscript/claude/`, pulled into Sections 2, 7 and 9 by three `\input` lines. It builds cleanly here at 17 pages (12 before); the reading copy is attached above. Nothing in the new text has had an independent reading, and nothing was committed.

**What went in**

- **Section 2 (entry).**
  - A doubling inequality at a reflection-invariant seam (Proposition 2.2) and its corollary for half-Hopf pieces.
  - Proposition 2.4: one relator tube in a Fuchsian conformally flat exterior closes up on the standard sphere.
  - The consequence: if every tube lies over a hemisphere, the construction cannot enter unless some conformal class on S²×S² has Weyl energy below three quarters of Kobayashi's conjectured infimum. This is conditional on that conjecture, which is open.
  - A short paragraph on symmetric fillings showing the hemisphere condition is needed.
- **Section 7 (rigidity).**
  - The strict Einstein range 4T/3 < e < 2T, citing the neck paper's "Strict half-harmonic bound".
  - Proposition 7.1: a Bach-flat class on S⁴ invariant under the rotations fixing a circle is round.
  - The remark that Euclidean Schwarzschild sits exactly at 2T.
- **Section 9.** Proposition 9.1, the logical form: the conjecture holds if and only if entry holds on every type and the sphere statement S holds.

**Things you should know**

- Proposition 7.1 is stronger than what my note had (SO(3) alone, not SO(3)×SO(2)), and its proof is new. The note now records it in a new section 9, and a fifth check script tests the formulas as printed (95 checks pass).
- I added one sentence to the abstract. Say so if you would rather it stayed as it was.
- Gursky's 1998 and 2000 theorems are cited from statements quoted by Fu and LeBrun; I did not read the primary texts, and I read only the abstract of Labbi. The source record at `references/claude/SOURCE_NOTES_REFLECTIVE_SEAMS_20261126.md` gives the level for each.
- I could not build on your computer from here, so your copy under `output/` is not replaced. `python3 tools/build_manuscripts.py master` should rebuild it.

- `chiral_weyl_energy_and_smooth_poincare.tex`: the abstract sentence, three `\input` lines, eight lines of provenance.
- `references/references.bib`: four entries appended.
